Cannon"Aap hi batayiye—tomorrow will be a reproduction of today? One peaceful day after another? Today’s Keihin Shimbun led with a hippo escaping the zoo. Tomorrow, perhaps, a panda giving birth?"

Kageaki"............"

Cannon"I thought not."
Cannon"Then we can get somewhere. If your country’s fate is troubling you, Mr. Minato, you ought to cooperate with GHQ."
Cannon"We can promise to free Yamato from Rokuhara’s misrule..."
Kageaki"............"

Not discrediting Yamato warriors this time.

To the point of making me wish he would kindly stop.

Kageaki"..."
Cannon"I am not insisting that you jump for joy. But you must have some ambition, surely? Having worked for Prince Maidono."
Kageaki"An ambition. Concerning what?"
Cannon"The world, perhaps? Complete the Pax Britannica, eradicate the disease of war from human history, raise society to a higher plane. To such a noble enterprise a man ought to devote himself."
Kageaki"Too large. And if I may say so, too much of a dream."
Cannon"Agreed. Badi badi baatein, and even my teeth are protesting. Let us come down to Yamato."
Kageaki"Yamato’s future."
Cannon"Yes. You cannot seriously think it best to let the Rokuhara shogunate continue enjoying its spring?"
Kageaki"And the best arrangement is for GHQ—the British Commonwealth—to enjoy the spring instead? I am to take that on faith?"
Cannon"A question of comparison, surely. Which spring is warmer for the Yamato people too?"
Cannon"I would not have thought it a particularly difficult choice."
Kageaki"Well... There are people who would sooner bow to a countryman’s sword than a foreigner’s gun."
Cannon"Pride before practical benefit? Beautiful, perhaps. I cannot call it wise."
Kageaki"Wise. To abandon the pride of an independent nation and live contentedly on the Queen charity—that is wisdom?"
Cannon"————"
Cannon"I can... understand what you are saying."
Cannon"But people generally do not think as you do. They would rather have comfort in servitude than pain with pride."
Cannon"Some understanding for those people is also necessary, I should say..."
Kageaki"............"
Kageaki"Understood. Let us allow that. Looking at the countries under British Commonwealth rule, one can indeed see more consideration for their citizens than under Rokuhara."
Kageaki"Having allowed it, I must add: I have no wish to back the losing horse either."
Cannon"Hmm?"
Kageaki"So far, Lieutenant Colonel, the future you have shown me amounts to pie in the sky. I cannot stake my life on this conversation alone."

en.html:
Cannon"...True enough. We have ample fighting strength. The money to keep it fighting... “ample” would be a generous description."
Cannon"So we intend to fight a short war. And... we shall manage it."
Kageaki"Even if Rokuhara uses its home ground as a shield and commits itself to not losing, rather than winning?"
Cannon"Given their disposition, I doubt they would find that decision easy."
Kageaki"They betrayed their homeland and endured the shame of submitting to your forces for the time being. If necessary, what means would they hesitate to use?"
Cannon"...I see."
Kageaki"Were I commanding Rokuhara’s forces, I would hold your offensive while diverting troops to Yokosuka. Yokosuka is the key to your supplies..."
Kageaki"Lose that, and the time in which you can operate becomes shorter still. There are limits to obtaining supplies locally. Capturing Fudaraku while you can still move would be all but impossible."
Kageaki"But fortify Yokosuka, and you have insufficient forces for the decisive battle. Again, driving out the shogunate army in a short time becomes a dream."
Kageaki"...And if, in addition, the reinforcements from the Philippines were intercepted at sea by the shogunate fleet—"
Cannon"............"
Kageaki"You would have to consider how to survive before considering the occupation of Yamato. Taken together... your position does not seem to me to permit such optimism."
Kageaki"What do you say, Lieutenant Colonel?"
Cannon"Hmm. Well... I will grant it."
Kageaki"..."
Cannon"A fairly sound analysis of the overall situation. If we opened hostilities this instant, matters would very likely develop as you say. A quick victory would be difficult."
Kageaki"If you want me in order to turn those poor odds into good ones, Lieutenant Colonel... I can only say you have selected the wrong man altogether."

景明 「……何の根拠もなく、そのお言葉を信じろ と？」
キャノン 「根拠ね。 　そうだな……もっともだ」
キャノン 「なら君は、根拠を得てから決断すればいい。 　……六波羅が事実上壊滅した後で、改めて 君を勧誘することにしよう」
キャノン 「君の協力はそれからでも構わないんだ」
景明 「…………？」
キャノン 「しかし…… 　その時になっても尚、君が決断を下せない ようなら――」
キャノン 「君は我々にとって必要な人間ではなくなる」
景明 「…………」
キャノン 「良き未来は努力を積み上げた山の上に。 　破局の結末は怠惰が沈澱する沼の底に」
キャノン 「必ずしもそうではないかもしれない。だが、 そう信じておくべきだ……人として生を全う するつもりがあるならね。 　違うか？　湊斗景明」
